untakenContent.description: A requirement whose content the accepted specifications do not hold, naming where the two differ and never what either says.

untakenRename.description: A rename the accepted specifications have not taken. acceptedHeading is null where the accepted requirement has no heading.

archive.description: The payload `htmlspec archive --json` (`patch archive`) writes, with --check and without: whether the change moved, and every finding archival asks about. A later 1.x release can add a property to any object in this payload, and only a major release removes, renames, or retypes one, so a consumer ignores a property it does not know.
archive.title: htmlspec archive --json

diagnostic.description: One diagnostic, as htmlspec_validate::StructuredDiagnostic writes it. The four optional fields are present only where the rule supplies them.

assets.description: The payload `htmlspec assets --json` (`get assets`) writes. A directory holding no asset store has nothing to check, and the operation writes no payload for it. A later 1.x release can add a property to any object in this payload, and only a major release removes, renames, or retypes one, so a consumer ignores a property it does not know.
assets.title: htmlspec assets --json

instructions.description: The payload `htmlspec instructions <stage> --json` (`get instructions`) writes: one workflow's instructions, as the program installs them. A later 1.x release can add a property to any object in this payload, and only a major release removes, renames, or retypes one, so a consumer ignores a property it does not know.
instructions.title: htmlspec instructions --json

change.description: One active change. state, total, tasks, and doneDifferently are present together, only for a change with a tasks document. follows is present only for a change that states a predecessor.

list.description: The payload `htmlspec list --json` (`get list`) writes, in one of three shapes: the active changes by default, the accepted specifications with --specs, and the runbooks with --runbooks. A later 1.x release can add a property to any object in this payload, and only a major release removes, renames, or retypes one, so a consumer ignores a property it does not know.

title.description: The runbook's tasks document's title, or its specification's where the tasks document has none. Absent where neither document states one.

version.description: The release the runbook's VERSION declares. Absent where the runbook has no VERSION a version can be read from.

list.title: htmlspec list --json

migrate-promote.description: The payload `htmlspec migrate promote --json` (`post promotion`) writes: the coverage gate's findings, the staged project's faults and diagnostics, and what was moved. A later 1.x release can add a property to any object in this payload, and only a major release removes, renames, or retypes one, so a consumer ignores a property it does not know.
migrate-promote.title: htmlspec migrate promote --json

migrate-survey.description: The payload `htmlspec migrate survey --json` (`get survey`) writes: every file an OpenSpec project holds, classified, and the facts a migration plan carries. A later 1.x release can add a property to any object in this payload, and only a major release removes, renames, or retypes one, so a consumer ignores a property it does not know.
migrate-survey.title: htmlspec migrate survey --json

preflight.description: The payload `htmlspec preflight <runbook> --json` (`get preflight`) writes: whether the runbook can start here, and every check it declares in document order. A later 1.x release can add a property to any object in this payload, and only a major release removes, renames, or retypes one, so a consumer ignores a property it does not know.

runbookRemedy.description: What the runbook says to do when this check does not pass: one line of text from a preflight/v2 declaration, present whenever the declaration carries one, whatever the outcome. It is the runbook's words, never run.

preflight.title: htmlspec preflight --json

diagnostic.description: One diagnostic, as htmlspec_validate::StructuredDiagnostic writes it. The four optional fields are present only where the rule supplies them.

preflightReport.description: The preflight report `run --as` writes in place of a run, when this machine does not satisfy every prerequisite the runbook declares and no record was created. It is the payload `htmlspec preflight --json` writes, with the same fields.

runbookRemedy.description: What the runbook says to do when this check does not pass: one line of text from a preflight/v2 declaration, present whenever the declaration carries one, whatever the outcome. It is the runbook's words, never run.

run.description: The payload `htmlspec run --json` (`post run`) writes, in one of three shapes: the run it started with --as, what every run recorded with --check, and the preflight report --as writes in place of a run when the machine falls short. A later 1.x release can add a property to any object in this payload, and only a major release removes, renames, or retypes one, so a consumer ignores a property it does not know.
run.title: htmlspec run --json

paragraph.description: One statement paragraph or scenario entry, as the view pairs it.

scenario.description: One scenario, as the view pairs it.

show.description: The payload `htmlspec show <change> --diff --json` (`get show`) writes: each requirement the change states, beside the accepted one where there is one. Every text is a list of runs labelled by the side that holds it. A later 1.x release can add a property to any object in this payload, and only a major release removes, renames, or retypes one, so a consumer ignores a property it does not know.
show.title: htmlspec show --diff --json

status.description: The payload `htmlspec status --json` (`get status`) writes: which of a change's artifacts exist, and how much of its work is done. A later 1.x release can add a property to any object in this payload, and only a major release removes, renames, or retypes one, so a consumer ignores a property it does not know.
status.title: htmlspec status --json

store-list.description: The payload `htmlspec store list --json` (`get registrations`) writes: every standalone project registered on this machine, and whether its location still holds a project. A later 1.x release can add a property to any object in this payload, and only a major release removes, renames, or retypes one, so a consumer ignores a property it does not know.
store-list.title: htmlspec store list --json

untakenContent.description: A requirement whose content the accepted specifications do not hold, naming where the two differ and never what either says.

untakenRename.description: A rename the accepted specifications have not taken. acceptedHeading is null where the accepted requirement has no heading.

sync.description: The payload `htmlspec sync --json` (`get sync`) writes: which of a change's requirements reached the accepted specifications, and which parts of its contract did not. A later 1.x release can add a property to any object in this payload, and only a major release removes, renames, or retypes one, so a consumer ignores a property it does not know.
sync.title: htmlspec sync --json

diagnostic.description: One diagnostic, as htmlspec_validate::StructuredDiagnostic writes it. The four optional fields are present only where the rule supplies them.

report.description: One document's report, as htmlspec_validate::StructuredReport writes it.

validate.description: The payload `htmlspec validate --json` (`get validity`) writes: the whole run, then one entry per document in discovery order. It is written even when a document cannot be read, and that document's entry carries `error` instead of `report`. A later 1.x release can add a property to any object in this payload, and only a major release removes, renames, or retypes one, so a consumer ignores a property it does not know.
validate.title: htmlspec validate --json
